messages:
maria_net: Heads up — customers in EU-WEST are reporting increased latency and a bunch of 5xxs for hosted inference routes. Seeing gateway 502/504 spikes starting ~08:07 UTC. @devon_oncall can you triage?

devon_oncall: On it. I see error spike in the dashboard: per-route error rate up x12, p90 latency up from 120ms -> 900ms. Auth failures also creeping up (~10% of failures show 401 then 502).

maria_net: Initial suspicion is cross-AZ path degradation between eu-west-az1 and eu-west-az3 causing retransmits. Packet counters on edge show intermittent drops.

ingrid_sre: Running quick traceroutes from edge -> provider uplink, got repeating * hop after ASN 64512:
```
traceroute to 34.56.78.90 (34.56.78.90), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.1.1.1  0.8 ms  0.6 ms  0.6 ms
 2  100.64.0.5  2.1 ms  2.3 ms  2.2 ms
 3  * * *
 4  203.0.113.45  120 ms 121 ms 119 ms
```
Looks like an upstream blackhole or flapping next-hop.

tom_support: Customer A (acct acme-inc) sent full request/response logs — saw repeated 502 then 401s for the same token, they said retries started failing. Opening CS escalation ticket and requested repro steps.

cs_bot: CS ticket #CS-34219 created, customer provided example curl: 
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Retry-After: 1
```
Customer also says SDK retry logic caused duplicated billing events for two API calls in a short window. Billing team pinged.

devon_oncall: I queued packet captures on the edge facing provider X and on the cross-az trunk. Capture shows bursts of dropped packets and TCP retransmits around 08:06:30-08:09:10 UTC. Also BGP adj flaps seen in provider syslog: `BGP: neighbor 203.0.113.45 reset` (multiple resets).

alex_platform: We pushed a tiny routing tweak last night to prefer az3 for eu-west traffic — could be amplifying the problem if that path is degraded. Rolling gateway route policy back to previous weights for eu-west now (will post rollback id).

deploy-bot: rollback-route-policy eu-west-weighting -> previous (deploy id rp-2026-473) started by @alex_platform at 08:12 UTC.

ingrid_sre: After rollback I see error rate dropping. p95 latency back down ~180ms, 5xx rate trending to baseline but still a few residual spikes. Packet drops reduced on trunk.

devon_oncall: Mitigation: (1) rolled route policy back, (2) temporarily divert heavy inference traffic to eu2 for customers with SLO-critical flag, (3) asked provider X for immediate triage with their NOC.

maria_net: Can we capture repro steps for customer and confirm billing duplication vector? Tom, can you share which SDK calls were retried and whether idempotency keys were present?

tom_support: Customer used SDK v1.3 without idempotency on generate calls. We flagged billing team to review duplicate charge window for acme-inc; billing assigned ENG billing-owner.

alex_platform: Provider confirmed BGP neighbor flapping due to a hardware module issue on their peering device (ticket with provider: P-98765). They applied a temporary hotspot configuration; vendor will replace module in maintenance window.

ingrid_sre: Post-mitigation checks: no packet loss in the 30m window, traces look normal. Keeping elevated monitoring for next 2 hours.

devon_oncall: Next steps: (1) update runbook with a cross-az routing rollback procedure (I will add), (2) confirm customer billing remediation plan, (3) schedule post-incident RCA with provider and net team.

maria_net: Thanks all. cs_bot — please update #customer-updates with a short note for acme-inc explaining mitigation and that billing team is investigating.

cs_bot: Posted customer update draft to CS thread and pinged billing.

tom_support: Will follow up with acme-inc on idempotency best-practices and offer to check their SDK usage to avoid duplicates.

ingrid_sre: Logging: saved pcap to investigations/1797001234-pcap.pcap, syslogs attached to incident ticket for RCA.

devon_oncall: Marking incident as mitigated for now. Keeping channel open for any regressions. :white_check_mark:
